message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find the Law | |-------|------------|-----------------------| | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and front‑seat passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Back‑seat seats are mandatory for children under 13. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.001–545.003 | | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• Rural highways: 70 mph (except 55 mph on certain roads).
• Urban roads: 35–55 mph depending on zone. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % for adults.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.041 | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way & Intersection Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• “Right‑of‑way” rules for merging, roundabouts, and school buses. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• No passing on either side of a stopped bus with flashing red lights. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other vehicles. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces, or on sidewalks.
• Pay‑meter and permit rules vary by city. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Annual registration renewal required.
• Vehicle inspections required in some counties. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.001 | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.001 | | **Special Situations** | • “No‑stop” zones, “no‑passing” zones, and “no‑turn” zones are posted.
• “School zones” have reduced speed limits during school hours. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | --- ### How to Find the Full Text of the Laws 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary source for all traffic laws. *Online:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TS/htm/TS.545.htm 2. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Provides driver’s handbook, safety tips, and updates. *Website:* https://www.dps.texas.gov/ 3. **Texas Legislature Online** – For legislative history and amendments. *Website:* https://capitol.texas.gov/ 4. **Local County or City Ordinances** – May contain additional parking, speed, or enforcement rules. *Check your city’s official website or county clerk’s office.* --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. - **Avoid distractions** – hands‑free only; no texting or handheld phone use. - **Observe speed limits** – especially on rural highways where limits can be higher. - **Be mindful of school zones** – lower speed limits and stop signs are common. - **Keep your vehicle in good condition** – regular inspections help avoid violations. --- #### Need More Specific Information? If you’re looking for details on a particular law (e.g., “What are the penalties for a first‑time DUI?”) or want to check how a recent amendment affects you, let me know and I can pull up the exact statute or provide a summary.
